promotion_rule: Repeated unexplained residual + distinct measurable dimension + negative boundary + falsifier + exact/semantic 3204 diff + R-F-R + explicit user review.

candidates.name: Delegated / Proxy Agency
source_signals: Ritual King: priests act under king authority
Child King: regents operate external cognition
Builder King: commanded work executed by others
candidates.definition: Degree to which an actor's intended control is realized through other agents while causal/role authority remains attributable to the originating actor.
candidates.activation_condition: Actor authorizes or owns an outcome but another actor performs material/operational execution.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not ordinary agency; requires separation between authority holder and executor.
candidates.falsifier: If authority, planning and execution all reside in the same actor, proxy agency is absent.

candidates.name: Shared / Distributed Authority
source_signals: Child King under regency: Power(shared)
Shadow King: co-regent or power behind
candidates.definition: Degree to which decision/control authority is simultaneously distributed across multiple actors rather than merely delegated from one uncontested controller.
candidates.activation_condition: Multiple actors possess non-trivial decision rights over the same role/result.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not delegation; no single actor necessarily retains complete authority.
candidates.falsifier: If one actor can unilaterally decide and all others only execute, classify as delegation instead.

candidates.name: Status-Capability Asynchrony
source_signals: Child King: full adult names/status while maturity is incomplete
candidates.definition: Gap between socially or institutionally assigned status/authority and the actor's current developmental or operational capability.
candidates.activation_condition: Role/status is granted before, after, or independently of matching capability.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not simple low capability; requires mismatch relative to an assigned role/status.
candidates.falsifier: If assigned status scales with actual capability and independence, the asynchrony is absent.

candidates.name: Public-Private Identity Divergence
source_signals: Court King: controlled public identity; private self not fully written
Shadow King: public face conceals private engine
candidates.definition: Degree to which an actor's publicly represented identity differs from privately held identity, motive, control state, or operative role.
candidates.activation_condition: Public representation and private operating state are systematically non-equivalent.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not ordinary audience adaptation; requires a meaningful identity/state divergence.
candidates.falsifier: If public representation and private operative state are materially aligned across contexts, divergence is absent.

candidates.name: Hidden Agency Expression
source_signals: Shadow King: invisible flow of decisions, true power signature elsewhere
candidates.definition: Capacity to exert causal influence while minimizing visible attribution of agency.
candidates.activation_condition: Outcomes track an actor's decisions but overt authorship/control signals are weak or intentionally displaced.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not merely private identity; this concerns causal control with low observability.
candidates.falsifier: If influence disappears when observable actions are removed, hidden agency is not supported.

candidates.name: Intergenerational Self-Extension
source_signals: Family/Dynastic King: self-model multi-generation
Father of Many: identity(lineage), succession charter
candidates.definition: Degree to which an actor represents descendants, lineage, or future generations as continuation of the self or its identity project.
candidates.activation_condition: Personal identity goals explicitly incorporate continuity through descendants or lineage.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not attachment alone; the descendant is represented as continuity of self/identity.
candidates.falsifier: Strong care for descendants without self-continuity representation does not satisfy this parameter.

candidates.name: Succession Security Motive
source_signals: Family/Dynastic King: succession document
Father of Many: fertility and succession charter
Child King: regency and future rule
candidates.definition: Motivational priority placed on preserving an orderly transfer of role, authority, lineage, or institutional continuity to a successor.
candidates.activation_condition: Actor choices are organized around continuity of role after replacement, death, retirement, or incapacity.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not generic family attachment or long-term planning; target is transfer of role/continuity.
candidates.falsifier: If successor identity is irrelevant to decisions, succession-security motive is absent.

candidates.name: Posthumous Identity Persistence Motive
source_signals: Architect of Eternity: name must survive when body is gone
Wise Elder: cartouches as remaining permanent self
Long-Reign: name outlasts body
candidates.definition: Motivational drive to preserve identity, name, reputation, representation, or influence beyond bodily life.
candidates.activation_condition: Actor invests resources in persistence of identity after expected bodily absence/death.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not general death anxiety; focuses on persistence of identity/representation.
candidates.falsifier: If post-death representation has no motivational effect on choices, the parameter is absent.

candidates.name: External Identity Anchoring
source_signals: Builder: permanent identity locked in stone
Composite: Identity Lock + External Memory
Cartouches repeatedly act as durable identity anchors
candidates.definition: Degree to which stable external symbols, records, names, objects, or institutions are used to maintain and retrieve a person's identity model.
candidates.activation_condition: Identity continuity depends materially on external representations rather than internal memory alone.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not external cognition generally; external artifact specifically stabilizes identity representation.
candidates.falsifier: If removing the external representation does not alter identity continuity/retrieval, anchoring is weak or absent.

candidates.name: Ritual Efficacy Belief
source_signals: Ritual/Priest King: repeated speaking/ritual is represented as maintaining power/order
Healer King: spoken name represented as protective
candidates.definition: Strength of belief that prescribed symbolic or ritual actions causally help maintain, restore, or alter a desired state.
candidates.activation_condition: Actor expects ritualized symbolic performance to have causal efficacy beyond its communicative/social role.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not belief/religiosity in general; requires causal efficacy attributed to ritual performance.
candidates.falsifier: If ritual is performed only for social convention with no expected causal effect, this parameter is absent.

candidates.name: Restoration / Order-Recovery Motive
source_signals: Restorer/Stabiliser: post-chaos restoration, healing flow of order
candidates.definition: Motivational priority to re-establish a previously valued order, identity, institution, or norm after disruption.
candidates.activation_condition: Current behavior is organized around returning a damaged system toward a represented prior acceptable state.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not resilience alone; resilience preserves function, whereas restoration specifically targets a represented prior order.
candidates.falsifier: If actor prefers novel replacement over restoring prior order, restoration motive is low.

candidates.name: Long-Horizon Self-Continuity
source_signals: Long-Reign: self-model over decades
Wise Elder: life-summary and backward/forward perspective
candidates.definition: Degree to which present decisions are integrated with a temporally extended self-model spanning long past and future horizons.
candidates.activation_condition: Actor treats distant past/future versions of self as strongly continuous with current self.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not planning alone; concerns identity continuity across time.
candidates.falsifier: Long-range plans made solely for external goals without temporal self-continuity do not establish this parameter.

candidates.name: Institutional Self-Extension
source_signals: Builder/Long-Reign/Empire profiles: identity persists through monuments, institutions, empire
candidates.definition: Degree to which an actor incorporates an institution, office, polity, or collective structure into the represented self and uses it as an extension of agency/identity.
candidates.activation_condition: Threats or achievements of the institution are processed as threats or achievements of the self beyond ordinary group membership.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not group belonging alone; institution functions as extension of self/agency.
candidates.falsifier: If institutional outcomes do not alter self-representation beyond ordinary membership effects, self-extension is unsupported.

candidates.name: Negotiated Parity Orientation
source_signals: Diplomat/Treaty King: negotiated balance of power, names standing equal
candidates.definition: Preference to stabilize conflict through reciprocal status recognition and negotiated equivalence rather than unilateral dominance or submission.
candidates.activation_condition: Actor accepts constraints/reciprocity to preserve a mutually recognized balance.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not generic cooperation; parity/status equivalence is a central target.
candidates.falsifier: If actor consistently accepts cooperation only under unilateral dominance, negotiated parity orientation is low.

candidates.name: Prestige-Model Adoption Susceptibility
source_signals: Worldwide Civilization: prestige architecture spreads through imitation of high-status language
candidates.definition: Tendency to adopt forms, practices, styles, or beliefs because they are associated with high-status actors or institutions.
candidates.activation_condition: Adoption probability rises with perceived prestige independent of intrinsic functional superiority.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not social learning generally; prestige of the model is the causal selector.
candidates.falsifier: If adoption tracks demonstrated utility while model status has no independent effect, prestige susceptibility is unsupported.

candidates.name: Golden-Age Loss Narrative Attraction
source_signals: Looks-Like Worldwide King: desire for a golden age that was stolen; lost paradise + erasure narrative
candidates.definition: Degree to which explanations framed as recovery of a superior lost past attract attention, meaning, or belief beyond their evidential support.
candidates.activation_condition: Lost/erased golden-age framing increases explanatory preference relative to evidence-matched alternatives.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not nostalgia alone; includes explanatory attraction to a lost-superior-past causal narrative.
candidates.falsifier: If lost-past framing provides no preference when evidence is held constant, the attraction is absent.

candidates.name: Collective-Capacity Underestimation Bias
source_signals: Ants Perspective: large monuments prompt extraordinary-agent explanations when collective labour, time, and organization are underrepresented
candidates.definition: Bias toward underestimating what coordinated groups can produce over long periods, thereby over-attributing large outcomes to extraordinary individual agents or mechanisms.
candidates.activation_condition: Observed output scale appears implausible because collective time/labor/organization is omitted or discounted.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not general incredulity; specifically mis-models collective productive capacity.
candidates.falsifier: If explicit collective-resource information removes the extraordinary-agent inference, the bias is supported; if not, another cause is needed.

candidates.name: Contextual Role-State Switching
source_signals: 18 King profiles treat one King as different functional brains under war, ritual, family, intrigue, diplomacy, ageing and other contexts
candidates.definition: Degree to which the same person's active self-model, priorities, affect and decision policy reorganize around a context-bound social/functional role.
candidates.activation_condition: A role/context change produces a coherent multi-parameter state transition without identity discontinuity.
candidates.negative_boundary: Not permanent personality change; the underlying person persists while an alternate functional profile activates.
candidates.falsifier: If parameter state remains unchanged across materially different roles, contextual switching is weak.

hard_guard: Exact-name noncollision is not sufficient to prove semantic novelty. Candidate remains review-required until semantic overlap and R-F-R are resolved.
